dedupe_keys.name: epa recycling infrastructure and market opportunities map version 2 0

description: This interactive map and its underlying data describe where the United States collects, sorts and processes recyclable materials and municipal solid waste. The US Environmental Protection Agency built it in support of the National Recycling Strategy to show existing infrastructure, generation and recycling of post-consumer material, and market factors. It locates 15 types of facilities, including material recovery facilities, glass, metal, paper, plastic, electronics and textile recyclers, landfills and transfer stations, each with name, address, county, contact details, NAICS code, infrastructure type and feedstock where known, and estimates tons generated and recycled by ZIP code for 16 material types, together with end markets, landfill tipping fees and bottle-bill deposits. Version 2.0, released in June 2025, moved the map to ArcGIS Online Experience Builder and consolidated the downloadable data files with instructions. As a US government product it is free to view and download, with no licence restriction stated. Caveats: data sources range from 2011 to 2021, most from 2018 to 2021, the estimates are modelled and not updated in real time, and facility lists may be incomplete. Simulation uses: building the facility layer of waste collection and recycling network flow models, checking which plants and landfills sit in flood or wildfire zones, and planning capacity for new recycling infrastructure. Related records: EPA's Facts and Figures on materials management (data-epa-sustainable-materials-management-facts-and-figures) gives national totals, and the EPA Disaster Debris Recovery Tool (data-epa-disaster-debris-recovery-tool) lists facilities for disaster debris.
